# Why Wsjr is spelled that way — and what it costs to get it right

There is no broken version of this name to repair. There is a record to preserve: **Wsjr**, exactly as the scholarly convention supports it.

The Osiris cycle is the best-preserved Egyptian myth, known from the Pyramid Texts onward: the good king murdered by his brother, the faithful wife who recovers him, the son who avenges him. It is simultaneously a story about kingship, about the flood that dies and returns, and about every human being who hoped to be judged worthy.

## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Wsjr
- **ASCII form:** osiris
- **Meaning:** "Mighty One (Egyptian wsjr)"
- **Domain of influence:** Afterlife, Resurrection, Vegetation
- **Pantheon:** Egyptian
- **Restoration:** ASCII-equivalent form
- **Original script:** 𓁥
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 405 of 597

## The Name Before the Marks


Spoken, the name runs `/ˈwɛzɪər/ (conventional)` — “WES-ir” — the form the Greeks heard as Ὄσιρις (Ósiris)

## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Wsjr** lives at [/osiris/](/osiris/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/osiris/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/osiris/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/osiris/patterns/).

The displayed form is ASCII-equivalent.

## Where the Name Stood First

The Osireion at Abydos, excavated by Naville and Frankfort, is a cenotaph-temple flooded symbolically with groundwater; the Dynasty XIX temples of Seti I preserve the finest Osiris chapels and the Abydos King List. Fourteen supposed relic-sites of his body were listed by the Abydos and Mendes traditions, giving a physical geography to the dismemberment myth. The temple on the web is the newest of these addresses — the first one that fits in a pocket.

## The Archetype at Work

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) seats this temple in **5 industries**, each match argued and weighted: **Agriculture, Food & Harvest** (the green god of the Nile's return: his resurrection is the flood that fertilises the field — agriculture's founding myth.); **Funerary & Memorial Services** (the weighing of the heart and the first mummy are the canonical warrant for every funerary rite after them — Osiris IS the judged dead.); **Waste, Recycling & the Circular Economy** (dismembered and reassembled, the god proved that what is broken can be made whole and fertile again.). The [Resonance File](/osiris/blog/resonance/) reads those seats through the myths themselves.

## In the Sacred Texts

The Egyptian tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [The Book of the Dead](/texts/book-of-the-dead/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
